- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast windows when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.4) — model fails to capture bearish momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag: true prices often dip below forecast 3–5 days after peak sentiment or spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model overcorrects downward, then undercorrects — leading to overshoots in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high for 3–7 days after a peak, ignoring sentiment decay.
- Sentiment decay >0.3 in 3–5 days correlates with forecast overcorrection — reduce forecast slope after sentiment drops below 0.5.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overestimate early days (1–7) and underestimate late days (24–30) — adjust for asymmetric decay.
